title: Reduction to extensions by zero and the Hom formula
statement:
Use the standing scheme setting [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]: $\ell$ is prime, $k$ is a field of characteristic $p>0$ with $p\ne\ell$, and $X$ is separated of finite type over $k$. Fix a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\pi_E$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Use the pulled-back condensed coefficient sheaf $\mathcal O_{E,T}$ on each small pro-étale site $T_{\mathrm{proét}}$ [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients, def-weil-pbc-small-proetale-site], and the categories $\Cons,\Dbc$ of [sk-def-sfb-constructible]. Work in the ambient unbounded module derived categories, with inverse/direct images as in [sk-def-sfb-module-pushforward-pullback], and the ordinary, uncompleted relative derived tensor and derived internal Hom of [sk-def-sfb-derived-tensor-hom], in the size convention [def-weil-size-convention]. Write $R\operatorname{Hom}_T(A,B)=R\Gamma(T,R\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O_{E,T}}(A,B))$ for global derived Hom, with derived sections as in [def-pur-ringed-site-zeroth-hypercohomology].

1. Every $C\in\Dbc(X,\mathcal O_E)$ admits a finite filtration by distinguished triangles [def-weil-triangulated-category] whose graded pieces are shifts of objects $a_!L$, where $a=i\circ u:S\hookrightarrow X$ is the inclusion of a stratum of a finite stratification [def-constructible-stratification], with $u:S\hookrightarrow Z$ open and $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ closed [def-weil-open-immersion, def-weil-closed-immersion]. Here $a_!:=i_*u_!$, with $u_!$ extension by zero [def-sfb-module-open-lower-shriek], and $L\in\Cons(S,\mathcal O_E)$ is pro-étale locally the completion of a finitely generated $\mathcal O_E$-module, meaning $\mathcal O_{E,S}\otimes_{\underline{\mathcal O_E}}\underline M$ for such an $M$. If $C\in\Cons(X,\mathcal O_E)$, the pieces may be taken in degree $0$.
2. For such $a,L$, let $R\underline\Gamma_Z:D(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\mathcal O_E)\to D(Z_{\mathrm{proét}},\mathcal O_E)$ be the derived support functor of [det-lem-formal-closed-support-derived], and put
$$L^\vee:=R\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O_{E,S}}(L,\mathcal O_{E,S}).$$
For every $K\in D(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\mathcal O_E)$ there is a natural isomorphism
$$R\operatorname{Hom}_X(a_!L,K)\simeq R\Gamma\bigl(S,L^\vee\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{\mathcal O_{E,S}}u^*R\underline\Gamma_ZK\bigr).$$
The object $L^\vee$ has Tor amplitude contained in $[0,1]$ (Tor amplitude as in [sk-def-sfb-constructible]). Tensoring with it commutes with small filtered colimits of complexes and with countable derived inverse limits. Filtered colimits are represented by degreewise colimits of module-sheaf complexes [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]; derived inverse limits refer to strict inverse systems of such complexes, with their total derived inverse limit and Roos triangle [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit, def-weil-derived-limit].

proof.text: The standing separated finite-type $k$-scheme and finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ satisfy the explicit opening hypotheses of [sk-lem-int-integral-heart]. By its clause (1), $C$ is bounded, each $H^q(C)$ lies in $\Cons$, and all its standard truncations stay in $\Dbc$. Apply [lem-pc-derived-lower-truncation-step-triangle] for the finitely many nonzero cohomological degrees: its triangle $H^{-n}(C)[n]\to\tau_{\ge -n}C\to\tau_{\ge -n+1}C\to H^{-n}(C)[n+1]$ expresses $C$ by finitely many extensions of shifted constructible sheaves. Thus it suffices first to filter a constructible sheaf $F$. Choose its finite adapted stratification $T_b$ from [sk-lem-int-integral-heart](2).

The finite-type hypothesis gives a finite affine cover with finitely generated coordinate algebras over $k$ [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and [lem-wf-affine-noetherian-components] makes each of these rings Noetherian. Thus $X$ is Noetherian. Apply clause (1) alone of [det-lem-coefficient-heart-common-stratification] to the finite adapted stratification (taking its unused coefficient parameter to be $E$). It gives a finite refinement of the underlying partition with open prefix unions $U_k=\bigcup_{h\le k}S_h$. This is a topological assertion; we do not apply its field-coefficient clauses (2) or (3) to integral sheaves. Put $Z_0=X$ and for $k\ge1$ give $X\setminus U_k$ the reduced induced closed subscheme structure supplied by [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme]. Choose each $S_k$ to be the open subscheme of $Z_{k-1}$ with underlying set $U_k\setminus U_{k-1}$. The remaining closed subscheme of $Z_{k-1}$ is $Z_k$: both reduced structures agree by uniqueness in that same lemma, and for $k=1$ it is the stated closed subscheme of $X$. We have $S_k\xrightarrow{u_k}Z_{k-1}\xrightarrow{i_{k-1}}X$ and $Z_m=\varnothing$. The standing scheme is Noetherian; its open complements, including those within the closed $Z_k$, are quasi-compact. The local-form assertion for the new scheme structures is established in steps 3-5, rather than inferred from topological containment.

Fix a refined stratum $S=S_k$ whose underlying set lies in an original stratum $T=T_b$. Form $W=S\times_XT$, with projections $v:W\to S$ and $w:W\to T$. By [lem-weil-pbc-immersion-base-change-lft](1), $v$ is an immersion. For every $s\in S$, the fibre $W_s$ is the fibre of $T\to X$ over the image of $s$, extended to $\kappa(s)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-immersion-fibre-degree-one], that original fibre is $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)$ because $x\in T$; its extension is $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)$. Thus $v$ is surjective. In its closed-then-open factorization [def-weil-closed-immersion], the open subscheme must be all of $S$, so $v$ is a surjective closed immersion.

Choose a pro-étale covering of $T$ on which $F|_T$ has its finite scalar-matrix local presentations, and pull the covering back along $w$ [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]. For $\Lambda=\mathcal O_E$, [sk-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients](1) makes module pullback exact, with the scalar action transported by $w^{-1}\mathcal O_{E,T}\cong\mathcal O_{E,W}$. Applying this exact functor to a presentation sends $\mathcal O_{E,T}^m\xrightarrow{A}\mathcal O_{E,T}^n\to F\to0$ to the identical scalar matrix over $\mathcal O_{E,W}$, with its cokernel. Thus $w^*(F|_T)$ has the same finite constant local models, including torsion; the scalar-matrix characterization is [sk-def-sfb-constructible](1). The composition isomorphisms of [sk-def-sfb-module-pushforward-pullback] identify this module with $v^*(F|_S)$, since both composites $W\to X$ agree.

Apply [lem-sfb-integral-model-surjective-closed-reflection] to the surjective closed immersion $v:W\to S$ of step 3 and the sheaf $F|_S$. Step 4 gives its hypothesis (b), so its conclusion (a) supplies the required finite integral constant local models on $S$ itself. This applies to every refined stratum, without assuming that its scheme structure factors through the original $T$. In particular $F|_S\in\Cons(S,\mathcal O_E)$ by [sk-def-sfb-constructible](2), taking the one-stratum stratification of $S$.

Apply [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-ringed-open-closed] on $Z_{k-1}$ with ring sheaf $\mathcal O_{E,Z_{k-1}}$ to $F|_{Z_{k-1}}$, open $S_k$, and closed complement $Z_k$. Push its short exact sequence forward along $i_{k-1}$, which is exact by that same node. Use the canonical coefficient-ring identifications and exact module inverse images of [sk-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients]. For $h_k:Z_k\hookrightarrow Z_{k-1}$, the composition isomorphisms explicitly stated in [sk-def-sfb-module-pushforward-pullback] give $i_{k-1,*}h_{k*}\cong i_{k*}$ and $h_k^*i_{k-1}^*F\cong i_k^*F$, and likewise $u_k^*i_{k-1}^*F\cong a_k^*F$. These are isomorphisms of modules with their transported coefficient actions; no equality of the module pullback with a bare sheaf functor is required. With $F^{(k)}=i_{k*}(F|_{Z_k})$, $F^{(0)}=F$, and $L_k=F|_{S_k}$, this gives
$$0\to a_{k!}L_k\to F^{(k-1)}\to F^{(k)}\to0.$$
Starting with $F^{(m)}=0$, these finitely many sequences exhibit $F$ as successive extensions of the $a_{k!}L_k$. All terms and pieces are sheaves in degree zero. By [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-triangle] the same sequences give distinguished triangles in the unbounded derived category.

Insert these filtrations, shifted by $[-q]$, into the finite truncation decomposition of step 1. Here is the elementary extension-refinement argument. For a distinguished triangle $A\to B\to D\xrightarrow{\delta}A[1]$ and a filtration $0=D_0\to\cdots\to D_r=D$, let $g_j:D_j\to D$ be the composite structure map and choose $B_j=\operatorname{Cone}(\delta g_j)[-1]$. Then $B_0\simeq A$ and $B_r\simeq B$ by the zero-map triangle and rotation of the original triangle. If $d_j:D_{j-1}\to D_j$ and $E_j=\operatorname{Cone}(d_j)$, then $g_jd_j=g_{j-1}$. Apply the octahedral axiom [def-weil-triangulated-category] to the composable maps $D_{j-1}\xrightarrow{d_j}D_j\xrightarrow{\delta g_j}A[1]$. Its cone triangle is $E_j\to B_{j-1}[1]\to B_j[1]\to E_j[1]$; shifting and rotating gives $B_{j-1}\to B_j\to E_j\to B_{j-1}[1]$. Append a filtration of $A$ to the chain starting at $B_0$. Induction on the finite number of truncation triangles therefore refines their shifted cohomology pieces by the shifted sheaf filtrations of step 6. Use one common ordered refinement for the finitely many cohomology sheaves in step 2, and apply the fibre-product comparison of steps 3-5 and localization sequences of step 6 to each sheaf on this refinement. This proves clause (1) with one finite stratification. When $C$ is a sheaf, step 6 already gives only degree-zero pieces. For $C=0$ or $X=\varnothing$ the filtration is empty.

Set $a_!L=i_*u_!L$ as in the statement. The coefficient $\mathcal O_E$ is admissible by [sk-def-localizing-closure]; the support adjunction [det-lem-formal-closed-support-derived](1), whose sheaf hypotheses include all those admissible rings, applies to the closed immersion $i:Z\to X$ with quasi-compact open complement. It gives naturally
$$R\operatorname{Hom}_X(a_!L,K)\simeq R\operatorname{Hom}_Z(u_!L,R\underline\Gamma_ZK).$$
Both sides are global derived Hom complexes: by [lem-sfb-derived-internal-hom-sections-model](2), applied on $X$ and on $Z$ (each module-object category over the pulled-back coefficients being the category of sheaves of modules over that ring sheaf on the small site), they are represented by global Hom complexes into K-injective representatives and agree with $R\Gamma(T,R\mathcal Hom(-,-))$ for the internal Hom of [sk-def-sfb-derived-tensor-hom], as in the statement. This is the stated derived support functor on the ambient module category, so no extension of a finite- or field-coefficient result is being assumed.

For coefficients $\mathcal O_E$, [sk-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients] gives the canonical natural isomorphism from $u^*$ to sheaf inverse image with module action transported through $\alpha_u^{-1}$. Transporting the exact adjunction $u_!\dashv u^{-1}$ of [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-ringed-open-closed] along this isomorphism gives the exact functors $u_!,u^*$ and their adjunction $u_!\dashv u^*$. Take a K-injective representative $J^\bullet$ of $R\underline\Gamma_ZK$, available by [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist]. Since $u_!$ is exact, [lem-weil-pbc-right-adjoint-preserves-kinjective] shows $u^*J^\bullet$ is K-injective. Termwise adjunction gives a canonical isomorphism of global Hom complexes
$$\operatorname{Hom}^\bullet_Z(u_!L,J^\bullet)\cong\operatorname{Hom}^\bullet_S(L,u^*J^\bullet).$$
These complexes compute the global derived Hom complexes of the statement: [lem-sfb-derived-internal-hom-sections-model](2), applied on $Z$ to the representative $u_!L$ and the K-injective $J^\bullet$, and on $S$ to $L$ and the K-injective $u^*J^\bullet$, says that they represent $R\Gamma(Z,R\mathcal Hom(u_!L,R\underline\Gamma_ZK))$ and $R\Gamma(S,R\mathcal Hom(L,u^*R\underline\Gamma_ZK))$, with $R\mathcal Hom$ the right adjoint of [sk-def-sfb-derived-tensor-hom]. Naturality in $K$ holds because maps of K-injective representatives compute derived morphisms [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived] and the termwise adjunction is natural in $J^\bullet$. Therefore
$$R\operatorname{Hom}_Z(u_!L,R\underline\Gamma_ZK)\simeq R\operatorname{Hom}_S(L,u^*R\underline\Gamma_ZK).$$
This argument imposes no boundedness assumption on $K$.

Clause (3) of [det-prop-sfb-qlbar-colimit-x-integral-limit], on $S$, identifies the pulled-back condensed coefficient ring with the completed ring sheaf $\mathcal O_{E,S}\cong\varprojlim_n(\mathcal O_E/\pi_E^n)_S$. Apply [det-lem-int-integral-heart-dualizable] on the scheme $S$ to the constructible sheaf $L$ (with its one-stratum local model). It says that $L$ is dualizable with derived dual $D=L^\vee=R\mathcal Hom(L,\mathcal O_{E,S})$, and $D$ has Tor amplitude in $[0,1]$. Apply [lem-sfb-dual-tensor-adjunctions] to this pairing. By symmetry of relative derived tensor, its right-tensor adjunction is $L\otimes^{\mathbf L}-\dashv D\otimes^{\mathbf L}-$. But [sk-def-sfb-derived-tensor-hom] defines $R\mathcal Hom(L,-)$ as a right adjoint of $L\otimes^{\mathbf L}-$. Uniqueness of right adjoints, including its evaluation-compatible comparison [det-sp-unique-right-adjoint], identifies the two right adjoints naturally:
$$D\otimes^{\mathbf L}M\simeq R\mathcal Hom(L,M).$$
Take $M=u^*R\underline\Gamma_ZK$, apply $R\Gamma(S,-)$, and compose with steps 8-9. This is exactly the corrected global Hom formula. Ordinary $\mathcal Hom$ cannot replace either derived internal Hom when $L$ has torsion.

For filtered colimits, choose a fixed flat-term K-flat representative $P^\bullet\to D$, as supplied by [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. For any small filtered diagram of module-sheaf complexes $M_\alpha^\bullet$, the termwise colimit represents the derived filtered colimit because filtered colimits are exact [lem-pc-module-filtered-colimits-tensor]. The same cited node gives
$$\varinjlim_\alpha\operatorname{Tot}(P^\bullet\otimes M_\alpha^\bullet)\cong\operatorname{Tot}(P^\bullet\otimes\varinjlim_\alpha M_\alpha^\bullet).$$
By the K-flat definition of relative derived tensor [sk-def-sfb-derived-tensor-hom] the two sides represent $\varinjlim_\alpha(D\otimes^{\mathbf L}M_\alpha)$ and $D\otimes^{\mathbf L}\varinjlim_\alpha M_\alpha$. This proves filtered continuity on the ambient unbounded category, without interpreting an ordinary categorical colimit in a triangulated category as a homotopy colimit.

For a strict countable tower $M_n^\bullet$, [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit] gives its functorial Roos triangle $R\lim M_n\to\prod_n^D M_n\xrightarrow{1-s}\prod_n^D M_n\to(R\lim M_n)[1]$, with products in the derived category. By [lem-sfb-dual-tensor-adjunctions], $-\otimes^{\mathbf L}D$ is a right adjoint and preserves those products; symmetry gives the same assertion for $T=D\otimes^{\mathbf L}-$. Derived tensor is exact: for a fixed K-flat model $P$ and a chain map $f:M\to N$, the map $\operatorname{Tot}(P\otimes\operatorname{Cone}(f))\to\operatorname{Cone}(\operatorname{Tot}(P\otimes f))$ is identity on $P^p\otimes N^q$ and multiplication by $(-1)^p$ on the shifted summand $P^p\otimes M^{q+1}$. The cone differential of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] and the total differential in [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves] makes this a chain isomorphism: on the shifted summand the horizontal differential acquires $(-1)^{p+1}$, the vertical differential becomes $-1\otimes d_M$, and the off-diagonal map becomes $(-1)^p(1\otimes f)$ on both sides. The inverse has the same signs. The shift comparison has the same $(-1)^p$ on the shifted factor. Thus tensor carries cone triangles and their shifts to distinguished triangles. Under the canonical product comparison, for every $n$ the $n$-th component of the transported $T(1-s)$ is $T(\mathrm{pr}_n)-T(f_n)T(\mathrm{pr}_{n+1})$, since tensor is additive. This is exactly the transition map $1-s_T$ for the tensored tower. Hence applying $T$ to the first Roos triangle gives the Roos triangle for $TM_n$. On the functorial resolution-and-cone models of the cited tower lemma this is the canonical comparison $T(R\lim M_n)\to R\lim TM_n$, and it is an isomorphism because the two product comparisons are isomorphisms. This proves countable derived-inverse-limit compatibility without assuming exactness of products of module sheaves.

proof_origin.place: Proof (1)-(2), corrected to use the derived internal dual; explicit ordered refinement, coefficient-independent nilpotent comparison, and colimit/Roos arguments.

split_report.summary: Q137 re-split for the human repair instruction of 2026-10-17. Statement and Lean records unchanged. Replaced the former 2316-character step 3 by the fibre-theorem comparison (existing node), elementary exact pullback of scalar-matrix presentations, and application of one new statement-only integral local-model reflection lemma. Retained the route and other proof arguments; adjusted their step references. The new lemma isolates cover lifting and descent of local isomorphisms rather than restating a clause of the item. All non-elementary steps are below 2000 characters. Read current cited statements and refreshed citations.
split_report.blueprint: Proof paragraph (1): steps 1-2 choose truncations and ordered strata; steps 3-5 expose the comparison and finite constant local-model descent previously hidden in old step 3; steps 6-7 give localization and finite filtration. Paragraph (2): steps 8-9 give the two derived adjunctions, step 10 the derived dual, and steps 11-12 filtered-colimit and strict-tower compatibility. The unit route is unchanged; cHom is the derived internal Hom macro, so no new statement dispute is raised.

tool_uses.why: Generic Noetherianity of finite-type coordinate algebras over a field, checking the hypothesis of the ordered-stratification tool.
Generic standard truncation triangles; no integral-unit node states the actual triangles.
Only coefficient-independent clause (1), finite open-prefix ordered refinement, used with auxiliary parameter E; field-coefficient clauses are not applied to integral modules.
Realizes the residual closed sets as schemes and identifies their reduced structures; no integral-unit node provides this scheme construction.
Generic immersion base change for comparing refined and original strata.
Generic cartesian coefficient identification, including integral coefficients, ensures exact pullbacks preserve scalar presentations.
Open-closed exact sequences, exact functors and open adjunction for arbitrary ring sheaves, hence for integral pulled-back coefficients.
Generic triangle from a short exact sequence of complexes.
Generic small-ringed-site K-injective resolution existence for an unbounded target.
Generic exact-left-adjoint criterion gives preservation of K-injectives by open restriction.
Generic K-injective calculation of derived morphisms in all shifts.
Generic evaluation-compatible uniqueness of the right adjoint identifies tensor-dual and internal Hom functors.
Generic ringed-site flat-term K-flat resolution; needed to compute integral tensor against a filtered diagram.
Generic exactness of filtered module-sheaf colimits and tensor-colimit comparison, rather than ordinary triangulated categorical colimits.
Generic functorial derived inverse-limit Roos model for module sheaves without exact products.
Generic identification of pulled-back condensed integral coefficients with the completed coefficient sheaf explicitly required by the current dualizability statement.
Generic fibre theorem for an immersion, used to establish surjectivity of the fibre-product comparison without an uncited residue-field argument; no integral Ext-unit lemma states it.

I tested it on id, Spec k -> Spec k[e]/e^2, and M=0, A and A/pi. A point of A^1 with j_!B shows surjectivity is needed. lean.statement: theorem integral_stratum_filtration (k : Type u) [Field k] [Fact (ringChar k).Prime] [Fact (ringChar k ≠ l)] (X : Scheme.{u}) [X.Over (Spec (.of k))] [LocallyOfFiniteType (X ↘ Spec (.of k))] [QuasiCompact (X ↘ Spec (.of k))] [IsSeparated (X ↘ Spec (.of k))] (C : integralDerived l E X) (hC : constantModelBoundedConstructible (integralCoefficientRing l E) X C) : ∃ (S : X.FiniteLocallyClosedStratification) (m : ℕ) (F : Fin (m + 1) → integralDerived l E X) (T : Fin m → Triangle (integralDerived l E X)), IsZero (F 0) ∧ Nonempty (F (Fin.last m) ≅ C) ∧ ∀ r : Fin m, T r ∈ Pretriangulated.distinguishedTriangles ∧ (T r).obj₁ = F r.castSucc ∧ (T r).obj₂ = F r.succ ∧ ∃ (a : Fin S.n) (Z : Scheme.{u}) (v : S.domain a ⟶ Z) (i : Z ⟶ X) (_ : IsOpenImmersion v) (_ : IsClosedImmersion i), v ≫ i = S.immersion a ∧ ∃ (L : pulledBackModuleObjects (integralCoefficientRing l E) (S.domain a)) (n : ℤ), IsConstantModelConstructible (integralCoefficientRing l E) (S.domain a) L ∧ HasFiniteConstantLocalModel (integralCoefficientRing l E) (S.domain a) L ∧ (DerivedCategory.homologyConcentratedIn 0 0 C → n = 0) ∧ Nonempty ((T r).obj₃ ≅ ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor _ 0).obj ((lowerStar (integralCoefficientRing l E) i).obj ((openImmersionLowerShriek (integralCoefficientRing l E) v).obj L))) ⟦n⟧)
